We show that the resulting topological classification depends on the parity of the number of half-twists: the sector index is a winding number for even parity, whereas only its parity is physically meaningful for odd parity, in which case the net director rotation is not quantised. We analyse the narrow-strip limit and solve the full two-dimensional equilibrium problem by finite-element methods. The competition between topological sectors depends on the strip aspect ratio and elastic anisotropy. In particular, for a single half-twist, the preferred sector changes at an aspect ratio of approximately 0.58, while for two half-twists two distinct minima of the same sector exchange their energy ordering near 0.60, without any change of topology. These results reveal how non-orientable topology and extrinsic curvature jointly shape nematic equilibria on curved substrates.

papers.title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)
papers.abstract: Agents based on large language models (LLMs) can now delete files and send payments on behalf of their users. News media reports routinely describe failures of these agents (e.g., Replit's coding agent deleting a production database), but a report often only says what went wrong and rarely (in)validates the incident or finds its root cause. Incident catalogs collect these reports, and benchmarks record whether agents fail, but neither replicates an incident nor tests the cause its report might identify. In this paper, we present ROGUE-AI (Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation), a multi-agent framework that closes the above gap and rebuilds each reported incident offline together with a matched control that lacks only the blamed cause, and runs agents on both. Our results suggest that ROGUE-AI is able to reproduce the reported harm in 89% of its 108 attempted replications. Agents built on five current GPT, Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek models made the reported mistake in 18% to 33% of runs, against at most 1% without the blamed cause. Of the 72 incidents with real-world harm, 62 had no underlying attacker, and in these, agents did what their task asked for but missed an ordinary hazard, such as a database shared with the live site. Replications without an attacker caused more harm than replications of prompt injection for all five models. Defenses against prompt injection look for injected instructions, but these replications contain none. Further, a warning after each tool output that names the hazard and its consequence lowered harm for all five models, whereas a note of the same length that does not mention the hazard left most of the harm in place. Built from real incidents, the ROGUE-AI replications form a reusable audit framework that vendors can rerun before each new release.

papers.title: Twisting Spinning Particles with Superghost Backgrounds
papers.abstract: We construct twists of spinning particles in the classical BV formalism by giving constant backgrounds to the bosonic ghosts of local worldline supersymmetry, in analogy with Costello and Li's twist of supergravity, which gives a nonzero background to the ghost of local spacetime supersymmetry. We represent the superghosts on polynomial states and gauge selected worldline R symmetries, imposing the shifted R constraints absolutely and the unshifted ones relatively. On flat targets, the N=2 particle, its N=4 extension on a complex target and an N=8 particle with two fermion flavors give the de Rham, Dolbeault and polynomial linear BCOV complexes. The last two are the linearized field content of the open and closed B-model target-space theories. Pairings and interactions require target-space input beyond the reduced worldline differentials.

papers.title: Multiplicative Sidon basis
papers.abstract: For a $h \ge 2$ integer a sequence of positive integers $A$ is called asymptotic basis of order $h$ if every sufficiently large positive integer $n$ can be written as a sum of $h$ elements of $A$. We say a sequence of positive integers $A$ is a multiplicative Sidon sequence if all the products of two elements of the sequence $A$ are distinct. In this paper we prove the existence of a multiplicative Sidon set which is an asymptotic basis of order 2 by using the probabilistic method.

papers.title: Edge cuts of bounded degree in sparse graphs
papers.abstract: Every simple graph on $n \ge 2$ vertices with at most $2n-2$ edges can be split into two nonempty parts with at most two crossing edges at each vertex. For $d \ge 3$ we bound the minimum number of edges in an n-vertex graph without a d-cut.

papers.title: MM-SystemOneBias: Evaluating Bias in Multimodal Jev-Style System One Decision Models
papers.abstract: When multimodal decision models determine actions, moderation outcomes, or quality judgments, their reliability depends on preserving semantic decisions across presentation changes, ignoring irrelevant additions, and distinguishing information consistent with task evidence from information that conflicts with it. Existing evaluations study decision-interface biases and multimodal model behavior in separate settings, leaving no common protocol to compare multimodal decision models with their backbones on practical tasks. We introduce \textbf{MM-SystemOneBias}, which evaluates 13 models on 5,323 original instances from nine public datasets and 11 task scenarios using six paired interventions: option order, option label, external judgment, image--text description, irrelevant information, and rating scale. Across seven matched decision-model--backbone pairs, decision models are more stable under option-label, irrelevant-information, and rating-scale changes in all seven pairs; six pairs also show lower option-order flip rates. They incur smaller accuracy losses under incorrect external judgments in all seven pairs and conflicting descriptions in six. In six pairs, they gain less accuracy from correct external judgments and show less favorable accuracy changes under consistent descriptions. Among pairs with unchanged semantic decisions, mean absolute changes in answer probabilities range from 4.56 to 11.55 percentage points, revealing input effects that accuracy alone misses.

papers.title: u3lib: An AI-Ready Computational Framework for U(3) Symmetry Algebra, Wigner Coupling, and Racah Recoupling Coefficients
papers.abstract: u3lib is a C++ library for U(3)/SU(3) representation-theory calculations in nuclear structure and related applications. It evaluates Wigner coupling and Racah recoupling coefficients using the procedure proposed in 2024 by Dang et al., which avoids the binomial coefficients and alternating sums used in earlier formulations. The library also provides irreducible representations (irreps), dimensions, Casimir invariants, conjugation, and tensor-product decompositions with outer multiplicities. It supports the canonical Gelfand-Tsetlin basis and the physical SU(3) $\supset$ SO(3) basis, including inner multiplicities and the transformation between the two bases. Generator routines return matrix elements in the canonical basis and reduced matrix elements in the physical basis. Python bindings mirror the C++ API. Domain skills supplied with the repository allow an AI assistant with code-execution access to call these routines from natural-language requests.

papers.title: Learning Control-Relevant Koopman Representations from Input-Output Trajectories
papers.abstract: Predictive accuracy alone does not ensure that data-driven Koopman representations are suitable for output-feedback control. This paper develops a continuous-time framework for learning control-relevant Koopman representations using only measured input-output trajectories. A causal encoder constructs the lifted state from a finite input-output window, and an additive lifted model is identified by integral regression. We distinguish observability, input-map compatibility, controllability, and data informativity. We characterize compatibility with a constant lifted input matrix, quantify input-map mismatch, and, under exact lifting assumptions, relate iterated Lie brackets to the controllable subspace of the lifted realization. A covariance-normalized finite-horizon observability criterion is optimized subject to separate bounds on output-prediction and temporal-consistency errors. Under the stated exactness and observability assumptions, the encoded lifted state depends only on the current nonlinear state. For approximate representations, we bound the difference between encodings of distinct past trajectories ending at the same state. An exactly liftable controlled system provides analytical ground truth, while a controlled Duffing oscillator illustrates the approximate setting, for which an informative exact additive lifting on an open set is shown to be impossible. On the exact benchmark, encoder initialization determines whether the learned representation recovers the analytical lift. In the reported Duffing experiments, observability promotion improves nominal Gramian measures without improving observer-based estimation or tracking, while updating the lifted-state estimate through the encoder at every sampling instant has a larger effect on tracking accuracy.

papers.title: Superluminal propagation in the magnetic NED reconstruction of the extremal Dymnikova black hole
papers.abstract: We reconstruct the magnetic nonlinear electrodynamics (NED) source of the Dymnikova geometry on the branch \(\Iinv>0\) and analyze its electromagnetic perturbations on the fixed background. The reconstruction does not admit a Maxwell limit. The extraordinary characteristic cone gives a transverse speed \(v_\perp^2=(3u-5)/2\), with \(u=r^3/P^3\), which becomes superluminal for \(r>r_{\rm lum}=(7/3)^{1/3}P\). The principal system is pointwise hyperbolic in the finite exterior \(r\ge r_e\), with positive local quadratic energy, but not uniformly hyperbolic up to spatial infinity. The radial effective potential admits an exact reduction, \(V_{\rm em}=f\ell(\ell+1)\mathcal{A}/r^2+ff_{,r}q +f^2(q_{,r}+\frac34q^2)\), behaves as \(V_0\proptoε^2\) near the horizon, and grows as \(27r^4/(4P^6)\) at infinity. It is numerically positive on a fine grid up to \(r=50P\). The Dymnikova reconstruction does not satisfy the hypotheses of the Tomizawa--Suzuki theorem, since it lacks a Maxwell limit, yet it still produces superluminal extraordinary photons. The reconstructed NED branch is therefore mathematically consistent as a source of the Dymnikova background, but not causally acceptable with respect to the physical metric in the asymptotic region. The global positivity of the effective potential and the quasinormal spectrum are left as open problems.

papers.title: Susceptibility source separation via Closed-form Alternating Newton-type Optimization
papers.abstract: Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping (QSM) provides a bulk magnetic susceptibility estimate per voxel, so contributions from paramagnetic and diamagnetic sources within the same voxel partially cancel. Susceptibility source separation methods identify these compartments by fitting a three-pool complex exponential model to multi-echo gradient-echo (GRE) data. However, conventional voxel-wise fitting with general-purpose constrained solvers requires several hours per whole-brain volume and often fails in high-susceptibility regions. We present CANON-QSM (Closed-form Alternating Newton-type Optimization for QSM), a solver that reformulates the subproblems of the three-pool model and solves them alternately via exact closed-form updates and Newton-type steps, yielding a substantial per-voxel computational speedup. Both in silico and in vivo evaluations demonstrate not only a massive reduction in reconstruction time, completing a whole-brain volume in under two minutes, but also improved accuracy and robustness against artifacts in high-susceptibility regions. Finally, an echo-time analysis of the three-pool model shows that source separation is driven by second-order nonlinearities in signal decay and phase evolution rather than first-order bulk estimates.

papers.title: Multi-institutional grading of Barrett's esophagus dysplasia without stain normalization using a pathology foundation model and multiple instance learning
papers.abstract: Barrett's esophagus dysplasia grading suffers substantial inter-observer variability, particularly for low-grade dysplasia, complicating clinical decision-making. We conducted a retrospective multi-institutional diagnostic accuracy study of a foundation model-based deep learning system for dysplasia grading, using 969 H\&E-stained whole slide images from four institutions. Patch-level classifiers trained on expert annotations identified diagnostically relevant regions, followed by attribute-aware multiple instance learning for slide-level classification as non-dysplastic Barrett's esophagus (NDBE), low-grade dysplasia, or high-grade dysplasia. On a held-out test set (n = 130), macro-averaged AUC was 0.96 (95\% CI 0.93--0.98). For binary dysplasia detection, sensitivity was 98\% (80/82) and specificity 81\% (39/48), with a negative likelihood ratio of 0.030 and quadratic-weighted \kap{} of 0.83 against expert consensus. No high-grade dysplasia case was misclassified as NDBE. Performance was consistent across institutions without stain normalization, indicating that stain-robust foundation-model representations may remove the site-specific preprocessing that has constrained prior systems to institution-specific deployment.

papers.title: You Have Mail: Set-Theoretic Types for Actors
papers.abstract: We present a type system for the processes of Elixir, a dynamic language based on the actor model whose static type system covers only its functional core. Each process is typed by $\mathtt{pid}(t)$, where the ``interface'' $t$ is the type of the messages the process expects in its mailbox: sends are checked against the recipient's interface, and receives rely on the interface of the process that performs them. One of the difficulties of typing Elixir is that mailboxes are implicit: a function shipped in a message may evaluate $\mathtt{self()}$ and execute receive instructions, and both refer to whichever process eventually runs the function---$\mathtt{self()}$ returns that process's pid, receive reads that process's mailbox---so the mailbox they act on is not known where the function is written. We solve this problem by inferring, for every function, bounds on the type of the mailboxes it can be used with; as a result, the system types higher-order functions that travel in messages even when they contain reference to $\mathtt{self()}$ and receive instructions. The only new annotation the programmer writes is the interface of each spawned process; everything else is inferred by reusing the existing subtyping and constraint-resolution machinery of Elixir, and the system is proved sound. For legacy code, the interface can be reconstructed from the receive clauses: what the branches do with their messages bounds it from above, and the most permissive solution is sharp enough to recover received pids and closures.

papers.title: GEOHunter: Mapping a Generative Engine Optimization Network in the Wild
papers.abstract: Generative engines synthesize retrieved web pages into answers, recommendations, and rankings. Generative engine optimization (GEO) services sell visibility in these answers by publishing promotional articles on user-generated-content (UGC) platforms for paying clients. Such promotion raises concerns in medical and financial domains, where misleading advice can cause harm. To study the severity of this problem, we measure one such paid-content operation across three major Chinese UGC platforms, uncovering 1,985 accounts associated with the network comprising 466,357 inferred promotional placements. We find that the network promotes products across diverse categories through a growing pool of accounts, conducting coordinated campaigns spanning months across multiple platforms while evolving its listicle content over time. Across nine generative engines from both the US and China, we find that 4.5% to 20% of retrievable cited pages are attributable to the network, depending on how strictly attribution is drawn. On eight of these engines, its clients are named in 52% of answers, against 68% for category leaders. Our work demonstrates the effectiveness of UGC GEO placement at influencing generative engine outcomes, and reveals content-level defenses as insufficient against coordinated UGC placements, where account-level and platform-level signals are necessary for proper defense.

papers.title: PhyDEX: A Benchmark for Physical Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models via Dynamic Extrinsic Dexterity
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have advanced rapidly in language-conditioned robotic manipulation, yet existing benchmarks mainly evaluate gripper--object contact and largely ignore how objects interact with the environment through gravity, friction, inertia, and mass distribution. As a result, it remains unclear whether current policies truly understand physics or merely interpolate from their training data. We address this gap through the lens of dynamic extrinsic dexterity and introduce PhyDEX, a throwing benchmark in which a robot must infer an object's mass, center of mass, and friction to send it to a destination beyond its kinematic workspace. PhyDEX contains 35K trajectories (143 hours) across nine tasks and 100 scenes, covering uniform, irregular, and dynamic-mass objects with static, multiple, and moving destinations. All data are generated by a scalable, fully automatic pipeline that combines grasp generation, motion planning, and closed-loop throw optimization under randomized physical properties. We evaluate three representative VLAs, GR00T N1.7, DynamicVLA, and ForceVLA, and find that all achieve success rates below 3\%. Our analysis reveals two key bottlenecks: limited robustness of pretrained models, which causes most failures before the throw, and physical blindness, as providing ground-truth physical properties roughly doubles success. Experiments on a humanoid robot and in the real world show the same failure patterns. We hope PhyDEX will drive the development of physically grounded robot policies.

papers.title: Topological notions of Shadowing under Semi-Conjugacy
papers.abstract: We study various notions of shadowing and investigate whether they are preserved under semi-conjugacy and inverse limits. In particular, we study Inverse shadowing, $H$-shadowing, Periodic shadowing, Ramsey shadowing, Density shadowing and Ergodic shadowing.

papers.title: Efficient and Variation-Tolerant Tree Inference via Compact and Scalable Mapping in Analog CAMs
papers.abstract: Tree-based machine learning methods are widely adopted for their interpretability and state-of-the-art accuracy on tabular data. These methods face efficiency challenges on conventional architectures due to irregular memory access patterns during tree traversal. Prior work uses analog CAM to accelerate tree traversal, but inefficient mapping requires exponentially more analog CAM columns as tree depth increases. Accuracy is also degraded by device non-idealities such as programming variations and soft decision boundaries. To address these challenges, we propose ACTIVAR, a compact variation-tolerant tree implementation in a dense analog CAM array via software-hardware codesign. On the software side, we introduce an analog-CAM-aware compact tree model that employs hierarchical subtrees with shared features to maximize hardware utilization. This dense mapping introduces redundancy, improving both model accuracy and hardware defect tolerance. Additionally, we develop Variation-Enhanced Training, which utilizes a fuzzy overlap boundary strategy to build models resilient to analog noise. On the hardware side, we design a FeFET-based analog CAM cell with a driver to sharpen decision thresholds and implement a pipelined multi-core architecture to optimize throughput and energy consumption. Across 13 classification and regression datasets, ACTIVAR maintains near-software-level accuracy while reducing hardware overhead by up to 99% compared with prior analog-CAM-based soft-tree designs. Under realistic hardware noise conditions, ACTIVAR limits accuracy degradation to just 3.7% on the MNIST dataset, whereas baseline models suffer a catastrophic 49.6% drop. Furthermore, the ACTIVAR architecture achieves energy efficiency gains ranging from $10^4$ to $10^6$ times over commercial general-purpose processors, establishing it as a highly efficient solution for high-capacity machine learning at the edge.

papers.title: Optimal Control in Pairs Trading with Negative-Power Utility
papers.abstract: We solve a finite-horizon consumption and investment problem in a pairs trading model with an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck spread and utility $U(x)=-x^{-γ}$, $γ>0$. Linearizing the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation gives explicit formulas for the value function and the optimal feedback control. A budget inequality and concavity verify optimality over all admissible strategies with nonnegative wealth on every finite horizon, without Novikov's condition. Under the optimal feedback, wealth and consumption admit deterministic upper bounds when the interest rate $r$ is at most the mean-reversion rate $κ$. If $r>κ$, each exceeds any prescribed level with positive probability at every time after the start. If $r>\sqrt{2+γ} κ$, there is an explicit critical horizon at and beyond which expected terminal wealth is infinite, while optimal expected utility is finite. When the critical time falls before maturity, expected wealth at that time is finite exactly when the initial spread is zero. We also show that the suprema of the negative powers of optimal wealth and consumption are integrable on every finite horizon exactly for orders $0<m\le 1+γ$.

papers.title: Text-Aware, Vision-Blind: How Multimodal Image Editing Systems Handle Unsafe Inputs
papers.abstract: Multimodal image generation systems have made rapid progress and increasingly emphasize content safety. However, their safety mechanisms tend to rely on a single modality and lack joint consideration of both visual content and text prompts, particularly in instruction-guided image editing, where the uploaded image may itself carry risk. We thus introduce EditSafetyBench, a benchmark that measures system-level safety awareness of advanced image editing systems, containing 5,940 image-instruction pairs, covering safe and unsafe images across 11 risk categories and three edit intents. We then probe the benchmark dataset on four systems, including Gemini, GPT, Qwen API, and Qwen Local. Based on our evaluation, we observe a systematic text-vision safety mismatch: Gemini and GPT refuse 87.1\% and 81.6\% cases containing unsafe-intent editing prompts, while only refusing 24.2\% and 22.4\% cases with both unsafe images and neutral instructions. At the category level, most risks are considered inconsistently by different systems, e.g., GPT allows 70.4\% editing attempts of unsafe political content while Gemini only allows 34.8\%. Notably, sexual content shows the strongest visual sensitivity, likely benefiting from mature NSFW identification works. Our findings highlight the need for safety guardrails that jointly reason over both visual and textual modalities in image editing systems.

papers.title: On Romik's rationality conjectures for critical percolation
papers.abstract: The completely packed $O(1)$ loop model can be viewed as an interface representation of critical bond percolation on the square lattice. We consider submatching events, which prescribe how these interfaces pair finitely many consecutive boundary points. Romik's rationality conjectures predict that the probabilities of these events on the semi-infinite cylinder are given by specific rational functions, which even become dyadic rationals in the half-plane limit. We derive explicit Pfaffian formulae for the probability of $k$ nested arches on the semi-infinite cylinder of circumference $2N$, valid for $k<N$. We deduce that these probabilities are rational functions of $N$ and, by taking the limit $N\to\infty$, that the corresponding half-plane probabilities remain rational. This establishes key aspects of Romik's conjectures. Our proof uses identities of Fonseca and Zinn-Justin, derived through the qKZ formalism, which express these probabilities as ratios of enumeration numbers for totally symmetric self-complementary plane partitions (TSSCPPs). These plane partitions admit a dimer representation, allowing us to apply Kasteleyn theory. We evaluate the resulting hypergeometric sum using Zeilberger's and Gosper's algorithms and then take the half-plane limit $N\to\infty$. Along the way, we derive a somewhat simplified expression for the inverse Kasteleyn matrix entries (encoding correlations in TSSCPPs) of Ayyer and Chhita, which might be of independent interest.

papers.title: Global regularity in optimal transportation under the A3w condition
papers.abstract: We prove global $C^{2,α}$ and $W^{2,p}$ estimates for potentials in optimal transportation under A3w condition. The cost satisfies condition A3w, and the domains are mutually uniformly $c$-convex with $C^2$ boundaries. We prove global $W^{2,p}$ estimates for positive continuous densities and we obtain global $C^{2,α}$ estimates for positive $C^α$ densities.

papers.title: Optimal Scheduling of Multi-Site AI Data Centers in Day-Ahead Markets
papers.abstract: AI data centers are among the fastest-growing loads on the power grid, and their flexibility is increasingly sought by grid operators. Using it requires a model that links what an operator controls, namely GPU power caps, job timing and job placement, to the power drawn at each site and the electricity prices it faces. This paper develops such a framework for a multi-site AI data-center fleet. It represents GPU power-cap levels; deferrable jobs with deadlines and inference with response-time headroom; and site facility power, and casts the fleet schedule as a linear program solved on day-ahead prices. A year-long simulation on 2025 California Independent System Operator (CAISO) day-ahead prices in three data-center markets demonstrates the framework. Coordinated scheduling lowers the fleet's energy cost by 6.3% at equal work. Four operating modes, each adding one capability, split this saving into efficient GPU operation that needs no price signal, price response in time, and routing work between sites.

papers.title: Neighbourhood Walkability and Cardiometabolic Morbidity in Greater London: A Fine-Grained Spatial Analysis
papers.abstract: Cardiometabolic diseases are leading causes of ill health, and neighbourhoods that support everyday walking may help reduce them. Studies often report lower disease prevalence in more walkable neighbourhoods. However, because walkability operates across multiple spatial scales, city-wide associations may conflate local neighbourhood form with broader metropolitan structure and co-varying environmental exposures. Here we show that while much of the walkability--morbidity association in Greater London operates through the city's macro-scale spatial structure, local alignment persists beyond it. Using an open five-component walkability index for 4,994 London census units and recorded prevalence of eight cardiometabolic conditions from primary-care registers, we found that higher walkability was inversely associated with all eight outcomes after adjusting for demographic composition and deprivation; one standard deviation higher walkability corresponded to 1.43 percentage points lower hypertension prevalence. Walkability followed a centre--periphery gradient, with a radial model explaining 74.2\% of its variation. Coefficients were reduced by 2--43\% within boroughs and 11--75\% after centre--periphery adjustment. After spatial-error adjustment, no clear association remained for obesity; coefficients for the other seven were reduced by 83--99\% relative to comparable log-scale models. Nevertheless, observed associations were more extreme than those from surrogate walkability surfaces preserving this spatial structure, for all eight outcomes in the primary analyses and for five after adjustment for nitrogen oxides. These findings caution against interpreting city-wide walkability coefficients as neighbourhood effects independent of wider metropolitan structure, and highlight the need for studies of neighbourhood form and health to disentangle global and local spatial structure explicitly.

papers.title: Classical Oracle Separation of QMA from the QCMA Hierarchy and Quantum Cryptography Even When P = QCMA
papers.abstract: Remark: This work is in submission at STOC'27 and thus the full manuscript has been publicly posted on the conference website since November 3rd, 2026. Inspired by the Codeword-Hash Structure problem recently introduced by Cakan (arXiV, 2026) to separate $\mathsf{QMA}$ from $\mathsf{QCIP}$, we introduce a new problem called Codeword-Hash pairs in Noise ($\mathsf{CHN}$) and prove that, in the query complexity model, it is in $\mathsf{QMA}$ but hard for the $\mathsf{QCMA}$ hierarchy $\mathsf{QCMAH} = \bigcup_{d\geq1}\mathsf{QCMA}^{\mathsf{QCMA}^{\cdots^{\mathsf{QCMA}}}}$, the classical-witness quantum-verifier analogue of $\mathsf{PH}=\bigcup_{d\ge1}\mathsf{NP}^{\mathsf{NP}^{\cdots^{\mathsf{NP}}}}$. Using this problem, we show that there exists a classical oracle ${O}$ such that $\mathsf{P}^{O}=\mathsf{BQP}^{O}=\mathsf{QCMA}^{O} =\mathsf{QCMAH}^{O} \subset \mathsf{QMA}^{O} \text{ but } \mathsf{QMA}^{O}\not\subseteq\mathsf{QCMAH}^{O},$ thus showing that quantum state or quantum proof advantage could exist even if classical computers can efficiently solve any problem that can be quantumly verified with a classical proof. Further, using our problem, we show that various quantum cryptographic primitives can exist even when $\mathsf{P} = \mathsf{QCMA}$ and thus neither quantum-computable one-way functions nor (verifiable) quantum computational advantage exist. In particular, relative to a classical oracle ${O}$ with $\mathsf{P}^{O}=\mathsf{BQP}^{O}=\mathsf{QCMA}^{O}=\mathsf{QCMAH}^{O}$, there exist pseudorandom states with classical keys and public-key encryption with copy-protected quantum decryption keys and classical public keys and ciphertexts, among other primitives, answering an open question of Kretschmer, Qian, and Tal (STOC 2025).

papers.title: Stochastic counterpart of Nesterov's method for sampling and provable non-acceleration of samplers with heavy-ball structure
papers.abstract: Polyak's heavy-ball method and Nesterov's method are two momentum-based methods that have inspired many optimization techniques used in applied fields, including machine learning. Momentum also provides a connection with sampling, and interestingly, many kinetic Langevin samplers reduce to the heavy-ball recurrence when velocity is eliminated and noise is removed. This observation motivates a natural question: what is the corresponding sampler for Nesterov's method? We propose a sampler whose deterministic part is exactly Nesterov's recurrence, driven by temporally correlated Gaussian noise and requires one new gradient evaluation per step. Noise correlation provides $\mathcal{O}(h^2)$ bias for smooth observables. We establish geometric ergodicity for possibly non-convex potentials. For strongly convex potentials with Lipschitz continuous gradients, we obtain contraction rates and show that, up to an additive constant, the energy decays at a rate of order $κ^{-1/2}$, where $κ$ is the condition number. For Gaussian targets, we show that relaxation has square-root dependence on $κ$. We further prove that any sampler based on heavy-ball dynamics with additive noise cannot achieve accelerated convergence uniformly over the class of strongly convex functions. Finally, we compare the proposed sampler with OBABO, BAOAB, HMC, MALA, BPS, and NUTS in numerical experiments and demonstrate the better performance of proposed sampler.

papers.title: Modeling the gravitational wave spectrum from slowly-evolving sources in the early Universe: constant-in-time and coherent-decay models
papers.abstract: We study the production of gravitational wave (GW) backgrounds from slowly-evolving sources in the early Universe, following the Constant-in-Time (CiT) model, presented and validated against simulations of decaying turbulence in arXiv:2201.05630. We extend the CiT model to account for the source decay using a coherent description for the unequal-time correlator (UETC) of the source. We present a generic framework that allows us to study different types of sources. As examples, we discuss the applicability of this framework to the production of GWs from decaying MHD turbulence, sound waves, and bubble collisions in first-order phase transitions. We show that the validity of the CiT and the coherent-decay models presented in this work relies on long decorrelation times of the source. However, as the decorrelation timescale of the UETC becomes short, a resonant term grows on top of the GW spectrum predicted by the CiT model, as found, for example, in earlier analytical studies of GW production from turbulence and sound waves. This model is compatible with previous numerical results and explains why sound waves in a radiation-dominated fluid are more efficient than subrelativistic MHD turbulence in producing GWs, which is no longer the case for relativistic turbulence. The CiT model predicts a generic spectrum that scales as $k^3$ in the IR regime, develops a linear $k$ at intermediate frequencies, and decays as $k^{1-b_Π}$ at frequencies above the inverse correlation length scale of the source, where $b_Π$ is uniquely determined by the type of source and the UV slope of its spectrum. Since the $k^3$ and $k$ scalings always appear for slowly-evolving sources and they are commonly found in studies of GW production, we motivate checking the potential applicability of the CiT to other sources of GWs.

papers.title: Classically Trained Quantum Generative Models with Shared Training and Fine Tuning for Quantum Matter
papers.abstract: Ground-state measurement statistics characterize quantum matter. Selected correlations can guide the classical training of a quantum sampler even when sampling the full distribution is difficult. We ask whether training across related ground-state distributions helps the sampler reproduce their correlations more accurately. We train a hypernetwork to map Hamiltonian parameters to circuit angles, sharing information across the phase diagram before local fine-tuning with additional reference data for quantum deployment. For classical training, we derive an unbiased Monte Carlo estimator of Fourier coefficients for circuits built from general Pauli rotations, with a cost that depends on the circuit generators. We also introduce a CDF-KL loss for comparing selected marginals. We study the Haldane Hamiltonian and transverse-field Ising model, using an automated search to select reference calculations near phase transitions. On the twelve-site chain, the adaptively pretrained hypernetwork matches the independent fits' final mean total variation distance in fewer local updates and continues to a lower error. On a 1,024-site chain and a 4 by 256 lattice, the fine-tuned circuits have lower squared maximum mean discrepancy from the reference distributions than the independent circuits at the evaluated point in each geometry. These results motivate shared training for preparing quantum samplers across a phase diagram and local fine-tuning.

papers.title: Activity-driven motion and deformation of a circular membrane domain
papers.abstract: Lipid bilayer membranes are nanometer-thin fluid interfaces characterized by both in-plane fluidity and lateral compositional heterogeneity. Cholesterol-rich liquid domains ("lipid rafts") are thought to regulate the spatial organization of membrane proteins and numerous cellular processes. While the passive diffusion and equilibrium shape fluctuations of membrane domains are well understood, much less is known about how the activity of molecular machines, such as protein pumps and enzymes, influences their mobility and deformation. Here, we analyze the dynamics of a membrane domain driven by an embedded molecular machine within the framework of two-dimensional Stokes flow. The molecular machine is modeled as a point singularity of the two-dimensional Stokes equations, including both rotational and irrotational singularities corresponding to force and source multipoles. We show that, despite being force-free, both force and source dipoles generate active flows that propel the membrane domain. For a force dipole undergoing rotational diffusion, the domain motion is diffusive at long times but exhibits a transient superdiffusive regime at intermediate times.

papers.title: Trimmed Branching Brownian Motion with Discontinuous Drift
papers.abstract: We consider a system of branching Brownian particles on the real line with bounded, possibly discontinuous drift $b$, and with a selection rule that removes one particle from the most crowded cells of a uniform partition of the line at each branching event so that the number of particles is preserved. As the number of particles tends to infinity, with the cell size tending to zero (sufficiently slowly), we prove convergence in probability of the empirical measure process to a deterministic limit characterized by the parabolic free obstacle problem $$\partial_tu=\tfrac12\partial_{xx}u-\partial_x(bu)+u-β.$$ Here the density $u$ has unit mass. Disintegrating the removal measure $β$ as $β_t(\mathrm{d} x)\mathrm{d} t$, the probability measure $β_t$ is supported on the spatial maximizers of $u(t,\cdot)$ for a.e. $t$. We establish existence and uniqueness of weak solutions in a suitable class of continuous densities, extending earlier results about this PDE to discontinuous drifts. We then consider an inverse problem: Given a target removal measure, find a drift for which the PDE admits a stationary solution with that removal measure. We show that this problem is solvable for every compactly supported Borel probability measure.

papers.title: Existence and Uniqueness of Mild Solutions to Rough Stochastic Partial Differential Equations driven by Fractional Brownian Motion with Hurst Index $H > 1/4$
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove a theorem on the unique solvability of the Cauchy problem for a stochastic partial differential equation driven by the fractional Brownian motion with Hurst index $H>\frac{1}{4}$.

papers.title: Amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves and applications
papers.abstract: We prove amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves in arbitrary dimensions. The proof uses the sharp square function estimates of Maldague and Guth-Maldague. As an application, we establish sharp small cap decoupling inequalities for the moment curve in every dimension $n\geq4$. This proves the conjecture of Demeter-Guth-Wang on exponential sums in all dimensions.

papers.title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm for Differential Equations: Application to Simulating a Biomolecular System
papers.abstract: Quantum algorithms for differential equations have the potential for substantial algorithmic speedups over classical methods. However, they rely on certain assumptions and abstract oracle specifications that leave their practical feasibility and computational advantages for realistic applications unclear. Here we formalize the concept of an end-to-end quantum algorithm for differential equations as one that accepts classical inputs and returns classical outputs, and provide implementations for algorithmic primitives in constructing such algorithms. We present a tailored end-to-end quantum algorithm for the linearized Poisson-Boltzmann (LPB) equation, a partial differential equation (PDE) with variable coefficients widely used in simulating a biomolecular system. We explicitly implement all aspects of the algorithm, from preparing an initial state to generating a quantum solution and estimating properties of the system. In particular, we develop a new discrete representation for variable-coefficient PDEs on a grid that enables efficient implementation of the operator oracle, and build on a recent technique based on optimal wavelet preconditioning to generate a quantum solution with a cost independent of the condition number of the discretized operator. We show the algorithm can be implemented by quantum circuits of size polylogarithmic in both the number of grid points $N_g$ and the inverse of the desired accuracy $\varepsilon$, with an overall gate cost polylogarithmic in $N_g$ and quasilinear in $1/\varepsilon$. We also show the classical preprocessing to construct the circuits has polylogarithmic cost in $N_g$ and $1/\varepsilon$. Our work provides a concrete end-to-end quantum algorithm for a PDE of practical value, demonstrates an exponential improvement in scaling with $N_g$ over classical methods, and provides a foundation for assessing its potential quantum advantage in practice.

papers.title: A Success Model at the End of Its Life Cycle: 30 Years of Regionalised Regional Rail in Germany
papers.abstract: On 1 January 1996, Germany transferred responsibility for regional passenger rail services from the federal government to the states. Three decades later, passenger-kilometres have doubled and competitive tendering has lowered operating costs substantially, making regionalisation the most successful element of the German rail reform. Its organisational model, however, has reached the end of its life cycle: tenders now attract on average only 1.3 bids, 26 contracting authorities and some 60 transport associations maintain overlapping structures, rolling-stock procurement has repeatedly shifted risk onto passengers, and since the Court of Justice of the European Union struck down the German track-access charge cap in 2026, funding no longer covers the ordered service volume. This article reviews the motives and results of regionalisation, identifies three structural design flaws, and argues for a second reform: consolidating authorities, standardising rolling stock, deciding between a repaired market model and integrated public operation, and indexing funding to real infrastructure cost development. The submission contains an English translation followed by the German original.

papers.title: Represented but misread: Post-training changes how language models read out what they represent
papers.abstract: Does post-training change what a language model represents, or how this representation is read out into an answer? We compared linear probes with the models' own answers, analyzed with signal detection theory, in six open-weight base models and their post-trained versions. For judgments of whether German texts were written by a human or an AI, probes and word n-gram classifiers separated the classes well, but the answers did not and often ordered the texts inversely. Post-training lowered the sensitivity of the answers on average ($Δd' = -0.34$ across model families; -0.29 across three prompts). It also changed the use of a stated base rate: Base models shifted their log-odds by less than the stated change in prior odds, most post-trained models by more. In two models with stage-wise checkpoints, the change occurred during supervised fine-tuning, model stitching implicated the early layers, and from mid-depth on internal states at positions after the text, not those of the text, transferred the change between checkpoints. Our corpora cannot be shared, so we add a case reproducible from public data, the truth of negated statements. Here, post-training acted in the opposite direction: Probes decoded truth at or near ceiling in every model, the answers of several base models did not use it, and post-training repaired them; by mid-depth the repair resided at the positions after the statement; below it, the representation of the statement contributed, strongly in one of four models. In a training study, adding 2,000 correctly labeled authorship judgments of news texts to otherwise identical fine-tuning data improved the answers on our newspaper and textbook corpora and inverted them on the chats, where they followed a news-trained probe of the base model. Post-training thus changed how a judgment is read out of what a model represents, and a small training signal can set its direction.

papers.title: Relativistic Kinetic Theory of Collisionless Particles with Variable Mass and Frame Transformations
papers.abstract: In this work, we present the relativistic kinetic theory of a gas of collisionless point particles with non-constant mass, which can also be understood as being subject to a scalar force. Our results hold in an arbitrary conformal frame, and we explicitly derive how they transform between frames. The mathematical construction relies on a tilted Sasaki metric, whose associated phase-space geometry is adapted to particles of variable mass, as well as on the one-particle distribution function, from which macroscopic observables are derived. Finally, we show that the one-particle distribution function can always be taken to be gauge- and frame-invariant, and the corresponding generalisation of the Liouville (or collisionless Boltzmann) equation is satisfied in each frame.

papers.title: ProtoDiffusion: Token-per-Layer Generative Modeling of Multi-Layer Images
papers.abstract: Graphic designs are ordered compositions of RGBA layers whose separation enables selection, movement, and reuse. Existing layered models represent each layer with a full-canvas or region-sized spatial latent grid, so representation size grows with the cumulative spatial extent of the layers. We present ProtoDiffusion, a latent-diffusion framework built on ProtoVAE, a multi-layer variational autoencoder that encodes a design into one shared spatial prototype and one candidate vector per layer. Each candidate conditions a shared decoder to reconstruct its corresponding RGBA layer. For $N$ layers, the representation contains $HW+N$ tokens before backbone-specific packing, compared with $NHW$ for full-grid-per-layer representations. ProtoDiffusion jointly denoises the prototype and a fixed set of candidate slots, conditioned on an image or text, with bounding boxes as optional layout guidance. The model leaves unneeded slots empty and determines the number of layers and, in absence of boxes, their layout, requiring neither as input. The same architecture supports both image-to-design and text-to-design. ProtoVAE achieves high-fidelity reconstruction from its compact shared latent representation, reaching 40.43 dB PSNR on layer crops. On the LayerD evaluation split, image-to-design achieves RGB L1 scores of 0.040 with bounding boxes and 0.057 without, with box-guided alpha soft IoU (0.850) comparable to the strongest fine-tuned baseline (0.871). On merged images, text-to-design reaches 66.41 FID versus 86.84 for FLUX.2 [klein], achieves a 0.860 text-accuracy score, and runs $19.1\times$ faster than the same-backbone generation-then-decomposition cascade.

papers.title: High-Accuracy Neural-Network Quantum States via Randomized Real-Time Dynamics
papers.abstract: Neural-network quantum states (NQSs) exhibit a disparity in converging to the ground state during energy minimization: while the energy converges quadratically with the error in the variational wave function, other observables converge only linearly, which limits the accuracy of physical predictions. Here we show how to close this gap by introducing a new algorithm that improves the accuracy of NQSs. Our method, termed dynamical averaging, estimates expectation values by averaging over a state (or observable) evolved in real-time. Using insights from quantum information, we prove an up-to-quadratic suppression of error in arbitrary ground state observables, thus matching the fast convergence of the energy. Importantly, this improved accuracy requires neither further energy minimization nor increased model complexity, but rather exploits the effect of randomization on quantum states. We demonstrate dynamical averaging on non-integrable spin models, where it accelerates convergence and substantially reduces errors in observables.

papers.title: Verify the Verifier: Specification-Grounded LLM Cross-Checking for Bugs That Escape UVM Scoreboards
papers.abstract: A passing UVM regression shows the design agrees with the reference model on what the scoreboard checks, not that it meets the specification. Bugs that pass every test yet violate the specification, termed scoreboard escapes, survive mature testbenches. We present Verify the Verifier, to our knowledge the first framework whose LLM-based Anomaly Cross-Checker examines a passing regression's traces against the specification. Of 564 bugs inserted into four OpenTitan IPs, 68 are candidate scoreboard escapes: non-equivalent, exercised by the tests, yet passing. The framework confirmed 41 as scoreboard escapes with assertions failing on the buggy design and proven on the original.

papers.title: Magnon high-harmonic generation by nonlinearities of spin torque driven by phonon-mediated crossing of many-body energy levels of bright and dark excitons
papers.abstract: Recent intense experimental focus on CrSBr, a two-dimensional (2D) antiferromagnetic semiconductor, has revealed numerous surprises in its response to ultrafast optical drive. We demonstrate that a single microscopic mechanism accounts for two of them---high-harmonic generation of magnons and persistence of magnon oscillations over \mbox{$\sim 1$ ns} time scale that is much longer than the femtosecond laser pulse (fsLP) pump duration. This mechanism arises from an unusually complex interplay of four different fundamental quasiparticles of condensed matter physics: magnons, optically bright and dark excitons, and phonons. By viewing magnons as the system and the other three quasiparticles as a quantum many-body bath, we derive an extended Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (eLLG) equation. Its new term generated by the bath is spatially nonlocal and time-dependent, as well as strongly {\em nonlinear} when the {\em crossing of many-body energy levels} of bright and dark excitons occurs via phonon mediation. It also resembles the so-called field-like spin-transfer torque (STT) in spintronics, but STT is driven there with current pulses, so it explains the microscopic origin of the recently experimentally conjectured {\em excitonic STT}. Since dark excitons supply energy to magnons long after the fsLP is switched off, such a reservoir opens avenues for its engineering and applications in optospintronics and optomagnonics, neuromorphic computing, and quantum transduction.

papers.title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. Global workspace theory (GWT) proposes that information is selected from parallel brain processes, integrated in a shared workspace, and made available to specialised processes. We introduce the Multimodal Concept Lens (MC-Lens), a multimodal Jacobian lens, to study these functions in VLM concept processing. Its vision encoder and language decoder lenses map intermediate states to a shared semantic space defined by the decoder's output vocabulary to compare concept accessibility across modalities. MC-Lens supports internal concept interventions to examine the role of accessed concepts in downstream computation. (i) Accessibility and selective access. Multimodal concept information is readable in intermediate states and selectively accessible as tasks require. We extend "readout carriers" from one name token to a token set to better capture and express concept information and support counterfactual experiments. (ii) Concepts in downstream computation. Counterfactual experiments show that accessed concept information participates in downstream computation and reasoning. (iii) Development of cross-modal alignment and selective access. We develop two J-space metrics tracking the development of cross-modal concept alignment more clearly than hidden state cosine in controlled VLM training. The experiment also shows that reliable selective access develops later than concept accessibility. (iv) Shared functions across models. Across VLM families and sizes, we find shared patterns of concept accessibility, query-dependent selectivity and cross-task intervention effects despite differences in internal organisation. These findings offer an experimental basis to study GWT in multimodal artificial systems and how it can guide cross-modal alignment improvements.

papers.title: Which black hole modes ring freely? Horizon regularity, the forced ringdown transient, and GW250114
papers.abstract: The quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a black hole are defined by keeping only ingoing waves at the horizon. We ask what horizon regularity requires of the outgoing waves this condition discards. For a scalar-like perturbation, bounded first derivatives in a frame regular at the future horizon rule out outgoing waves that decay more slowly than the surface gravity $κ$, and smoothness singles out a ladder of frequencies, $ω=mΩ_{\rm H}-ijκ$ with $j=1,2,\dots$ and $Ω_{\rm H}$ the horizon angular velocity. We call these the horizon modes. For Schwarzschild black holes and the dominant $\ell=m=2$ Kerr modes, only the fundamental QNM decays more slowly than $κ$. These local statements leave the QNM spectrum unchanged but matter for merger ringdowns, because a source falling through the horizon drives the exterior at the horizon frequencies. Each QNM then has a driven and a free part, and the free part takes over only once the driving decays faster than the mode. The fundamental mode separates from the driving early. The overtones stay driven until the source is hidden behind the potential barrier, so overtone amplitudes fitted near the signal peak are in general not those of free oscillations. In GW250114, a ringdown model of the fundamental mode plus the first horizon mode, $ω=2Ω_{\rm H}-iκ$, is preferred over the fundamental mode plus its first overtone, with Bayes factors between 2 and 30, for start times from $2M_f$ before to $8M_f$ after coalescence. The horizon-mode fit returns a remnant that is heavier and spins faster than the inspiral predicts, as expected from nonlinear backreaction: the horizon that emits the mode has not yet settled to its final mass and spin. Zero-noise injections of numerical-relativity-calibrated waveforms reproduce both the preference and the shift, which are therefore features of general relativity.

papers.title: Realized versus Population Reliability: Anytime-Valid Self-Consistency Certification under Correlated Reasoning
papers.abstract: Self-consistency certification treats repeated sampling from a language model as sequential evidence accumulation and stops when an anytime-valid e-process crosses a threshold, guaranteeing finite-sample Type I error control by Ville's inequality. Prior constructions assume sampled rollouts are conditionally independent. We show this assumption fails in practice: reasoning streams are positively correlated through shared reasoning prefixes or across-prompt heterogeneity, changing not merely certificate efficiency but the hypothesis certified. Modeling dependence via a per-unit latent state (the random-effects / intraclass-correlation structure) induces exchangeable, equi-correlated increments with correlation $ρ$. Correlation splits the single null into a realized null about the drawn belief and a population null about average model behavior, which coincide only when $ρ=0$. We show: (i) the standard betting e-process remains anytime-valid for the realized null, not the population null; (ii) read as a population-null test, a suitable mixture has asymptotic crossing probability at least $π=P(μ(Z)>0)$, potentially exceeding nominal $ε$; (iii) the within-unit mean's effective sample size saturates at $1/ρ$, so extra within-unit rollouts cannot restore population validity; and (iv) a prompt-level e-process restores population validity, with optimal allocation at one rollout per prompt under a pure rollout budget. Simulations and Claude Haiku 4.5 rollouts confirm this regime dependence: on GSM8K ($\hatρ=0.435$, $\hatθ=+0.96$) the gap is dormant, whereas on AIME ($\hatρ=0.480$, $\hatθ=-0.15$) the single-unit rule crosses on 24% of prompts at nominal $ε=0.05$, while the prompt-level procedure declines (0.00). This correctness result identifies which reliability claim an anytime-valid certificate actually supports under dependence.

papers.title: Star-forming disc galaxies align tangentially with the cosmic tidal field
papers.abstract: The alignments of galaxy shapes, with one another and with the large-scale structure of the Universe, have been a topic of considerable investigation within cosmology and extragalactic astrophysics for the last 60 years. Galaxy alignments are a major systematic for weak gravitational lensing and help us learn about the processes of galaxy formation. Red early-type galaxies are known to show strong radial alignments around other galaxies; however, blue star-forming galaxies have shown little evidence of alignment. We combine SPHEREx spectrophotometry with DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys to build a full-sky catalogue of 71 million galaxies with precise redshifts. With this catalogue we are able to measure alignment signals by splitting galaxies into colour and morphological samples. We detect tangential alignment of blue disc galaxies at $22.5σ$ and radial alignment of red spheroidal galaxies at $65σ$. By measuring the alignment signal separately around overdensities and underdensities, we show that each of these alignments has the scale and environmental dependence of a linear response to the cosmic tidal field; a response purely quadratic in the Gaussian tidal field, as in classic tidal torque theory is ruled out.

papers.title: UV Bounds on Inflationary Parity Violation
papers.abstract: A question of fundamental interest is whether parity is violated on large scales in the Universe. This possibility has been motivated by recent analyses of the four-point matter correlation function. It has also been suggested that detectable parity violation could be generated during inflation by the dynamical Chern-Simons operator, a leading effective field theory correction to general relativity. In this work, we examine this possibility in realistic UV completions, including fermionic and string-theoretic examples. We show that existing bounds on the tensor-scalar-scalar (TSS) bispectrum strongly constrain the possibility of generating a detectable parity-odd trispectrum. For tensor-to-scalar ratios near current observational limits, detectability is incompatible with, or pushes against, the regime of validity of these UV completions. A detectable signal can remain possible for a sufficiently small tensor-to-scalar ratio, but only at the cost of an extremely large enhancement of the TSS vertex. Thus, while a future search for large scale parity violation is worth pursuing, generating a detectable signal within a consistent effective theory is highly nontrivial.

papers.title: Coda-DaVinci: Reimagining Video Generation with Code2Video
papers.abstract: Code2Video uses agent-authored 3D proxies to guide video generation, enabling explicit control over structure and dynamics. However, how to construct proxies and prompts for optimal downstream quality remains underexplored, as do the capabilities and limitations of this paradigm. Through controlled experiments and blinded human evaluation, we study proxy granularity, physics simulation, and prompting. The results reveal task-dependent trade-offs: coarse proxies favor natural motion, while medium-grained proxies favor consistency. Physics simulation and proxy-aligned prompting further improve average quality. Guided by these findings, we introduce Coda-DaVinci, a task-adaptive agentic framework for Code2Video generation that selects between proxy-guided and direct generation, adapts modeling granularity to each entity, and coordinates simulation with proxy-grounded prompting. Its multi-agent harness preserves scene assets and guides repairs through visual inspection and independent review. Experiments demonstrate leading instruction following on VTR and scene consistency on R2M, improved physical plausibility over direct generation, and higher visual realism than the compared Code2Video baselines. Long-video evaluations further show gains in event structure and consistency across successive interactions, while revealing limitations in transition stability and adherence to scene settings.

papers.title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robotic vision-language-action (VLA) models can execute diverse individual manipulation skills, yet they still struggle with long-horizon loco-manipulation tasks, where temporal structure, skills, and precision are tightly coupled within a monolithic model. We propose Physically Grounded Execution (PGX), a framework that offloads temporal and precision control to two classical training-free components, allowing the VLA to focus on stage-specific skill dynamics. PGX decomposes long-horizon loco-manipulation into three layers: (i) a predicate-based state machine governs task progression, using physical predicates to gate phase transitions, trigger recovery, and coordinate navigation and waiting. Shared predicate semantics connect offline demonstration segmentation, online execution, and stage-wise evaluation; (ii) VLA skills operate within active manipulation phases, with flat or stage-trained models concentrating on task-relevant actions; and (iii) world-coordinate locking (WCL) maintains spatial consistency through base station keeping, object-relative positioning, and world-anchored contact targets. We demonstrate the effectiveness of PGX with extensive experiments conducted on three simulated tasks and one real-world task using a Unitree G1 humanoid robot for long-horizon loco-manipulation, showing improvements in stage progression and task success rates. Project page is available at: https://kl-research.github.io/pgx

papers.title: Equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for congruence subgroups of level 2
papers.abstract: The modular properties of holomorphic Eisenstein series for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and its congruence subgroups do not carry over to their primitives. Instead, the transformation of iterated Eisenstein integrals under congruence subgroups of level $N$ introduces inhomogeneous terms comprising (among others) cyclotomic multiple zeta values of level $N$. We combine iterated Eisenstein integrals for the congruence subgroups of level $N=2$ of arbitrary iteration depth with their complex conjugates and (single-valued) level-2 cyclotomic multiple zeta values such that they define non-holomorphic modular forms. Our construction of these so-called equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for $Γ(2)$ and $Γ_0(2)$ proceeds at the level of generating series that take values in an infinite-dimensional (pro-unipotent) Lie group and closely follow Brown's analogous construction in the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ case. The required insertions of cyclotomic multiple zeta values are controlled by zeta generators for level 2 that normalise the corresponding (pro-nilpotent) Lie algebra of the generating series and whose Lie-bracket relations we determine systematically. Upon restriction to Eisenstein series of modular weight~2, we recover single-valued multiple polylogarithms on the genus 0 modular curve $Γ(2)\backslash \mathbb{H}$.

papers.title: Active Feature Acquisition by Distilling an Oracle Teacher
papers.abstract: Acquiring every feature of an instance is often costly: a measurement can carry a monetary price, a time delay, or a privacy cost. Active Feature Acquisition (AFA) addresses this by learning a policy that decides, per instance, which features to acquire under a budget. Existing AFA methods train this policy by optimizing a self-constructed utility target rather than distilling an explicit teacher. We construct this teacher explicitly. At training time the label and the unobserved feature values are available, and together they determine the teacher in closed form: an oracle that ranks every candidate by its effect on the downstream predictor's error. OracleImitator distills this ranking into a deployable policy by soft-target imitation. Across multimodal medical diagnosis and the AFABench benchmark, OracleImitator matches or outperforms existing AFA methods across the budget range, recovering 90% of the attainable accuracy gain at under a quarter of the acquisition cost. Because the teacher is an explicit algorithmic object rather than an implicit optimization target, we can also measure directly how much of its ranking is recoverable by a policy restricted to what is visible at deployment.

papers.title: Local orbital magnetization and Chern markers from equilibrium local currents
papers.abstract: Local currents carry the orbital magnetization of a macroscopic sample and are key for modeling inhomogeneous magnetic materials and for understanding magnetoelectric and topological responses. However, producing realistic simulated images of local currents in inhomogeneous systems remains challenging. Building upon recent work on stochastic estimation methods for tight-binding models, we show that all matrix elements of positive semidefinite operators defined on a lattice can be obtained at once from a single set of filtered random vectors. This eliminates the need for independent simulations previously required for off-diagonal elements, which significantly speeds up the calculation of spatial maps of local currents. Further, we express bond currents in terms of loop currents that obey a discrete Poisson equation, with the current vorticity acting as the source term. Its solution yields a local orbital magnetization. In analogy with the global Středa relation, the derivative of this magnetization with respect to the chemical potential defines a new local Chern marker. Built entirely from bond currents, it requires no position operator and is not bound by the zero-sum rule of projector markers in open samples. Hence, it is free of boundary-compensation artifacts, and its sample average converges to the bulk Chern number in a controlled fashion.

papers.title: A Tutorial on Complementarity-Based Contact Models for Robotics
papers.abstract: Simulating rigid-body dynamics with contact is fundamental to robotics, from motion synthesis and control to mechanism design. Many widely used simulators rely on cone complementarity formulations, whose physical assumptions and numerical solution require substantial background. While excellent surveys, monographs, and course notes exist, they mostly address computational mechanics or computer graphics or document a single simulator. To the best of our knowledge, a self-contained pedagogical treatment for robotics, bringing these formulations and their solvers together with complete derivations and a unified notation, does not yet exist. This tutorial addresses this gap by connecting rigid-body dynamics, conic optimization, and frictional contact. In particular, we explain how complementarity conditions encode non-penetration and frictional dissipation, determining separation, sticking, and sliding without prescribed contact modes. We distinguish equivalent transcriptions from convex relaxations, showing how the latter can introduce artifacts such as lift-off and creep. We examine the existence and uniqueness of motion and contact forces, including the solver's role in selecting among multiple solutions. We then compare first-order and Newton-based methods, explain regularization and proximal strategies, and discuss trade-offs between computational cost, robustness, and physical fidelity. Connections to widely used simulators, optimal control, and differentiable simulation help readers interpret simulation results, choose suitable formulations and solvers, and develop their own contact dynamics routines.

papers.title: SoK: Assessing the Evolution of LLM Capability in Software Vulnerability Research
papers.abstract: LLM-based agents are becoming increasingly capable at discovering, validating and patching vulnerabilities in real software, and vendors and researchers report that this is already changing how vulnerabilities are found and fixed. These claims, however, are scattered across papers, vendor reports and disclosures and are rarely comparable. We introduce a framework that rates these capabilities on an autonomy scale modeled on the levels of driving automation, and qualifies each claim by its correctness, its availability and the strength of its evidence. We use this framework to systematize the published evidence on LLM capability in vulnerability research. We find that agents discovered, validated, and patched vulnerabilities in real-world software without human intervention before the restricted frontier models of 2026, and that open-weight models subsequently attained comparable autonomy for discovery and validation. We then measure the consequences of evolving LLM security capabilities in a decade of public vulnerability records, advisories and exploitation data. In 2026 the number of disclosed vulnerabilities more than doubled, with an increasing share rated critical or high, and severe bugs that had survived a decade or more in widely used code were reported several times more often than before. Yet the time between the stages of a vulnerability's life, from report to fix and from disclosure to attack, has not shifted noticeably so far. We grade the mitigations proposed in the literature with an explicit rubric and draw guidance for each group of stakeholders from the best-supported ones.

papers.title: An Efficient Algorithm for Matroid Cups
papers.abstract: We design a polynomial-time algorithm for matroid cups with $O(1)$ discrepancy. Our matroid cups algorithm design consists of a sequence of reductions to simpler instances, culminating in $O(n)$ instances of matroid cups where the matroid has rank 1.

papers.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
papers.abstract: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. To overcome this trade-off, we train a single, scalable network that processes both images and video and predicts depth maps at native resolution. Depth Pro 2 produces depth maps that are metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent all at once, outperforming prior work in all of these dimensions. We release a family of models that define a new Pareto frontier in terms of metric accuracy, sharpness, temporal consistency, and runtime. We release code and weights at https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-depth-pro-2/

papers.title: Scalable Simulation of Strongly Correlated Fermions with Neural Gaussian Tensor Networks
papers.abstract: Accurate simulations of strongly correlated electrons remain a central challenge in computational physics. We introduce neural-network Gaussian projected entangled-pair states (NN-GPEPS), which exploit the locally-entangled subspace of Gaussian states to give an architecture more compatible with modern neural networks and an exact contraction cost of $O(N^{3/2})$ on two-dimensional lattices. For the Hubbard model at $U/t=8$ and $1/8$ hole doping, we obtain state-of-the-art variational energies in large lattices of up to 1024 sites. These results demonstrate an accurate approach to strongly correlated fermions by connecting neural networks with Gaussian tensor networks.

papers.title: Fast, in-place, and ancilla-free quantum algorithms for integer multiplication and inversion
papers.abstract: Arithmetic operations are a fundamental building block in the design of quantum algorithms, with their implementation cost expected to have a significant impact on the viability of a wide variety of quantum applications. In this work, we present novel algorithms for a number of in-place quantum arithmetic operations that are highly efficient in terms of their space and gate count overheads compared to the current state-of-the-art. We show that in-place modular multiplication of integers, modulo a power of two, can be performed with either a classical or quantum odd multiplier using $O(n^{1+ε})$ gates and no ancilla qubits, for any $ε>0$. We then show that standard in-place integer multiplication can be performed with a non-zero classical or quantum multiplier using $O(n^{1+ε})$ gates for any $ε>0$, with no ancilla qubits required for the classical multiplier and a logarithmic number of ancilla qubits for the quantum. Using our quantum modular multiplication algorithm, we also show that in-place modular inversion, modulo a power of two, can be performed using $O(n^{1+ε})$ gates and no ancilla qubits, for any $ε>0$. To our knowledge, these are the first quantum algorithms achieving both subquadratic gate counts and sublinear ancilla counts for each of the considered in-place operations. All but one of these fast operations are optimal in terms of memory, only requiring enough space to store the output of the operation, which overwrites the input directly. We present our multiplication algorithms as consequences of a single unified theorem, which may find further application within quantum arithmetic.

papers.title: Query-Optimal Quantum Minimum Finding from Numerical Estimators
papers.abstract: We propose a quantum minimum-finding algorithm for objectives accessed via numerical estimators that avoids the logarithmic query overhead of amplifying the confidence of estimates before the search. A coherent estimator that is $\varepsilon$-accurate with probability at least $2/3$ on each of $N$ labels suffices to find a $2\varepsilon$-optimal label using $O(\sqrt N)$ base-estimator queries at constant confidence. The query bound and the additive-error constant are separately worst-case optimal. More generally, suppose a preparation assigns probability mass at least a known $p$ to objective values at most $a$. Without knowing $a$ or the prepared distribution, our algorithm returns a candidate and an estimate $v$ such that, jointly with constant probability, $v$ is $\varepsilon$-accurate for the candidate and $v\le a+\varepsilon$. The algorithm uses $O(p^{-1/2})$ queries to each of the preparation and estimator oracles in the worst case, and the selected candidate can be retained as a quantum state. For preparation width $s_P$ and estimator workspace width $w$, it requires $O(s_P+w+\log\log(4/p))$ qubits, independently of the requested confidence. Applications give worst-case optimal $Θ(\sqrt N/η)$ queries for selecting an $η$-optimal bounded expectation, and guided ground-energy estimation using $O(ω^{-1})$ preparations and $O((ωη)^{-1})$ elementary controlled-evolution queries at constant confidence, where $ω$ is a lower bound on the guiding state's ground-space amplitude overlap.

papers.title: Bio-PM-Guided Synthetic IMU Generation
papers.abstract: Collecting and labeling inertial measurement unit (IMU) data for human activity recognition (HAR) is expensive, and models trained on one group of subjects often fail to generalize to unseen individuals. Even with balanced data, classifiers struggle to distinguish dynamically similar activity classes and benefit from targeted augmentation. We explore whether synthetic IMU data generated in the representation space of a pretrained biosignal encoder, Bio-PM \cite{b1}, can serve as a practical augmentation source. Rather than synthesizing raw signals, we leverage Bio-PM's frozen encoder to convert 10-second IMU windows into token embedding sequences and train class-conditional decoders in this space: (1) an autoregressive transformer decoder that predicts tokens sequentially, and (2) a diffusion decoder that learns the token distribution through a denoising objective. We analyze generation realism through distributional metrics and embedding-space visualizations, evaluate downstream utility through leave-one-subject-out HAR classification, and present a PatchDecoder for approximate raw waveform reconstruction. Our diffusion decoder achieves a Train-on-Synthetic-Test-on-Real (TSTR) macro-F1 of 0.68, demonstrating that generated tokens are realistic enough to train a classifier that transfers to real data. Combining synthetic-token augmentation with a 320-dimensional gravity-aware feature representation raises LOSO macro-F1 from 0.729 to 0.809 over a real-only baseline across 51 subjects on the WISDM benchmark, with statistically significant gains concentrated in the most challenging activity classes. These results demonstrate that high-fidelity generation in a pretrained encoder's representation space is achievable and practically useful for cross-subject HAR augmentation.

papers.title: Local velocimetry for atomic superfluids: from Riemann rarefaction waves to quantized vortices
papers.abstract: We demonstrate local velocimetry for atomic superfluids in two dimensions (2D). Using matter-wave interferometry based on Raman--Bragg beam splitters, we map the local gradient of the phase of the superfluid's wavefunction onto displacement of the interference fringes and reconstruct the 2D velocity field. We illustrate the capabilities of this technique by applying it to two canonical problems. First, we directly observe the self-similar evolution of the velocity field in 1D Riemann rarefaction flows. Second, we map out the full 2D velocity field around quantized vortices, explicitly demonstrating the quantization of velocity circulation.

papers.title: Variants of Beam Search for DiskANN
papers.abstract: Graph-based data structures such as DiskANN, HNSW, and NSG constitute the state of the art for large-scale approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search. Indyk and Xu introduced the notion of $α$-reachable graphs, which include graphs built by DiskANN's slow-preprocessing construction, and proved that greedy search achieves an approximation factor of $\tfrac{α+1}{α-1}$. Independently, Al-Jazzazi et al. proposed adaptive beam search (ABS) with a relaxation parameter $γ> 0$, showing a $\tfrac{2}γ$ approximation on navigable graphs ($α\approx 1$), where greedy search admits no guarantees. In this work, we unify and generalize these results by proving that ABS with parameter $γ$ on $α$-reachable graphs achieves an approximation of $\tfrac{α+1}{α(γ+1)-1}$ for any metric. Moreover, on sorted $α$-reachable graphs (introduced by Gollapudi et al.) under the $\ell_2$ metric, we obtain the tighter bound $\max\bigl(\tfracα{α(γ+1)-1}, \tfrac{α^{2}+1}{α^{2}(γ+1)-1}\bigr)$. Beyond these theoretical results, we design a beam predictor using features inspired by fine-grained analysis of ABS, trained via a constrained objective that minimizes mean distance computations subject to a target recall.
